target_customer: Consumers shopping for used cars who wanted one search across Craigslist, dealer sites and other classifieds
problem: Used car listings are scattered across many sites, so buyers cannot easily compare prices and find deals in one place.
business_model: Free consumer search engine, with revenue plan not stated in sources found
product_category: Used car search and price comparison

founders.name: Christopher Berner
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as the only founder; no bio on the page.

founders.name: Dwight Crow
founders.background_notes: Named by VentureBeat (2012-10-01) as one of the two founders and only teammates; not listed on the YC page.

exit.reason: Founders were hired by Facebook in October 2012 and said they would seek a buyer for the service; CB Insights lists a December 2012 sale to Ark.

technical_complexity.rationale: Crawling and indexing classified listings and normalizing prices is standard scraping and search work that two founders could build, though keeping access to sources was fragile.

defensibility.rationale: The product depended on listings owned by others and Craigslist blocked its indexing, so there was no data or network moat.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: VentureBeat (2012-10) reports Craigslist blocked Carsabi from indexing its car listings, and traffic reportedly halved. Facebook hired the founders but did not buy the service.

market_need_then: Used car buyers had to search many classified sites. The founders said they started in October 2011 to simplify used car buying (VentureBeat, 2012-10-01).

branding.domain_note: Used carsabi.com; the domain's later history was not found. Ark.com, Inc. holds a CARSABI trademark filing.

brand_strength.rationale: No press about the brand itself, no community or merch found; the name was a coinage with no sourced origin.

outcome_analysis: Carsabi launched at the March 2012 YC Demo Day with two founders and almost no outside money. Craigslist blocked indexing of its listings and traffic reportedly halved by autumn, so the product depended on sources it did not control. In October 2012 Facebook hired both founders without buying the service, and a database lists a December 2012 sale of the brand to Ark.com. The cause of inactivity is the founders' move to Facebook after platform blocking, not a publicly stated shutdown reason.
notes: Company site carsabi.com did not resolve from this environment, treated as dead or unreachable. CB Insights lists $20K raised over 3 rounds with investors Ark, Meta and Y Combinator; only the 2012-03-27 seed row is dated, and the figures rest on a single database. The Ark acquisition rests on CB Insights plus a trademark record owned by Ark.com, Inc.; VentureBeat says Facebook did not acquire the service. No dated competitor source was found near the March 2012 batch, so the list is empty; Craigslist is a listing source and blocker, not recorded as a competitor. Exit conflict: the directory says Inactive while sources report a founder acquihire and a sale of the brand to Ark; the product itself appears abandoned.
